metadata.note: Utility teardown of runtime/scripts/fill_slates.py — a 155-line safety-net that walks every reel in books/ and stamps a FormACard onto every SLATE BEAT: beat that has no media/<bid>.mp4, no manim/<bid>.mp4|mov, no silent flag, and no shot.remotion.pattern yet. Dry-run by default; --apply stamps + shells out to remotion_scenes.py to render → media/<bid>.mp4, then shells out to run.sh to recompile the review cut. Precise slate definition lives in slate_resolves() and find_slates(). The stamp is fixed: pattern='FormACard', props={lines:[headline], dark:false}, headline = _truncate(narration_text, words=11) (with … if trimmed), fallback to beat.name or beat_id. Discovery: reels are found by walking HERE.parent (books/) for every dir containing youtube/<slug>/beat_sheet.json — an explicit --books override lets the caller point at a disposable fixture. Node PATH pulled from ~/.nvm/versions/node/latest via _node_env(). Historical anchor (docstring): SlateCard was DELETED 2026-08-26 by Bear's order — DESIGN-PRINCIPLES §1 banned the eyebrow/kicker + bold-sans-headline + rule + decorative-circle card. Slates now fill with the Form A card: serif lines only, no chrome, no redundant act-name echo. beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — the whole pipeline in one horizontal phase-flow. WALK books → FIND slates → STAMP FormACard → RENDER (remotion_scenes) → RECUT (run.sh).
beats.narration_text: The pipeline. One invocation. Walk books slash for every reel that has a beat sheet. Find the slate beats — no media, no manim, no silent flag, no pattern. Stamp each one with a Form A card whose lines are the first eleven words of the narration. Then shell out to remotion scenes dot py — the slate renders to media slash B whatever dot mp4. Then shell out to run dot sh — the review cut recompiles. Dry run is the default. Apply is the flag.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 2 — slate_resolves() + find_slates(): the precise definition of a slate beat.
beats.narration_text: What counts as a slate. Slate resolves returns true only if the beat has no media slash B whatever dot mp4, no manim slash B whatever dot mp4, and no manim slash B whatever dot mov. Find slates walks the beats in the sheet. It also skips two more cases — a beat marked silent, and a beat whose shot dot remotion dot pattern is already set. So a slate is: no rendered video, no explicit pattern, not silent. Four conditions.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 3 — stamp_slates() + the _truncate() headline helper. The FormACard is the only pattern this tool writes.
beats.narration_text: The stamp. For every slate beat, take the narration, truncate to eleven words with an ellipsis if it's longer, fall back to the beat's name and then to its ID if the narration is empty. Write that string into shot dot remotion dot pattern equals Form A Card, props equals lines colon headline, dark colon false. Provenance and version get stamped alongside. Then the whole sheet is written back — atomically, one dot json write.

props.title: fill_slates.py:34-106 — helpers + stamp_slates()
props.code:
def _truncate(text: str, words: int = 12) -> str:
    parts = text.split()
    if len(parts) <= words: return text
    return " ".join(parts[:words]) + "…"

def _topic(sheet: dict) -> str:  # unused in current version
    meta = sheet.get("metadata", {})
    return (meta.get("topic") or meta.get("series") or
            meta.get("book") or "").upper()

def stamp_slates(reel: Path, slates: list, sheet: dict):
    changed = False
    for b in slates:
        bid = b["beat_id"]
        headline = _truncate(b.get("narration_text",""), words=11)
        if not headline:
            headline = b.get("name", bid)  # fall back to name -> bid
        shot = b.setdefault("shot", {})
        shot["remotion"] = {
            "pattern":    "FormACard",
            "provenance": "proven-core/FormACard",
            "version":    "1",
            "props":      {"lines": [headline], "dark": False},
        }
        changed = True
    if changed:
        (reel / "beat_sheet.json").write_text(
            json.dumps(sheet, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False))
    return changed
props.sparkLine: One pattern only: FormACard. Serif. No chrome.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 4 — render_reel(): the two subprocess calls. remotion_scenes.py first, then run.sh. Any non-zero exit is a FAIL line.
beats.narration_text: Render reel. Two subprocess calls. First — python remotion scenes dot py, pointed at the reel. It reads the beats, finds the ones with a pattern set, renders each to media slash B whatever dot mp4. Second — bash run dot sh, same reel. It rebuilds the slate review cut. Every non zero exit code becomes a FAIL string with the last three hundred characters of stderr. The main loop treats any FAIL as a reel failure and prints it — but keeps going.

props.title: fill_slates.py:109-130 — render_reel()
props.code:
def render_reel(reel: Path, env: dict) -> list:
    acts = []
    r = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable,
         str(HERE / "scripts" / "remotion_scenes.py"),
         str(reel)],
        env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        acts.append(f"REMOTION FAIL: {(r.stderr or r.stdout)[-300:]}")
        return acts
    acts.append("remotion: ok")

    r = subprocess.run(
        ["bash", str(HERE / "scripts" / "run.sh"), str(reel)],
        env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        acts.append(f"ART_RUN FAIL: {(r.stderr or r.stdout)[-300:]}")
        return acts
    review = reel / f"{reel.name}-slate.mp4"
    sz = f"{review.stat().st_size // 1024}K" if review.exists() else "missing"
    acts.append(f"recut: {review.name} ({sz})")
    return acts
props.sparkLine: Two shell outs. One try-hard order.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 5 — falsifiability. What can go wrong. REMOTION FAIL vs ART_RUN FAIL vs missing-beat_sheet vs already-fully-filled.
beats.narration_text: Failure modes. Four. One — the beat sheet doesn't exist. Find slates returns an empty list and None. The reel is quietly skipped. Two — remotion scenes exits non zero. Render reel appends REMOTION FAIL with the last three hundred characters of stderr, and never even calls run dot sh. Three — run dot sh exits non zero. ART underscore RUN FAIL, same shape. Four — no slates at all. The loop reports zero affected reels and does nothing. One bad reel never takes the batch down.

# 1. no beat sheet — find_slates returns ([], None) — reel silently skipped
def find_slates(reel):
    if not (reel/'beat_sheet.json').exists():
        return [], None

# 2. remotion_scenes exits non-zero — render_reel bails BEFORE run.sh
if r.returncode != 0:
    acts.append(f'REMOTION FAIL: {(r.stderr or r.stdout)[-300:]}')
    return acts   # never reaches run.sh

# 3. run.sh exits non-zero — recut fails, review mp4 not refreshed

    acts.append(f'ART_RUN FAIL: {(r.stderr or r.stdout)[-300:]}')
    return acts

# 4. main loop — nothing to fill

(no bulleted reel lines follow)

# main loop's status test — 'FAIL' in any action string flags the reel:

beats.role_note: VERDICT — the whole surface as an artifact card, six lines.
beats.narration_text: So — fill slates dot py. The safety net. One walk of books slash. One rule for what counts as a slate — no media, no manim, no silent flag, no pattern. One stamp — Form A card with a truncated headline. Two shell outs — remotion scenes, then run dot sh. Dry run is the default. Apply is the flag. Silent beats and pre patterned beats are never touched. That's the whole tool.

props.artifactHeading: fill_slates.py — the whole surface, in the order it does its job
artifactLines: input — books/ (default) or one reel path; --apply flips out of dry-run.
define — a SLATE is a beat with no media/manim mp4, not silent, no shot.remotion.pattern.
find — walk every book/youtube/*/beat_sheet.json; collect slate beats per reel.
stamp — shot.remotion = FormACard with lines=[truncate(narration, 11 words, …)].
render — shell out to remotion_scenes.py, then run.sh — non-zero exits print FAIL.
output — one report line per affected reel; the recut review mp4 refreshes on success.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer. Prompt read aloud verbatim, then discussed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code, pointed at a books directory of your own that has at least one reel in mid build. Ask Claude to run fill slates in dry run against that folder. Then have Claude READ the printed reel-slash-beat list and pick one slate to author properly — a real Remotion pattern, not a Form A card fallback. Fill slates is the SAFETY NET for what didn't get authored. Every time you accept its stamp you lose a bit of teaching. So use it, then replace it beat by beat.

props.command: Point Claude Code at a books/ tree with at least one reel currently in mid-build. (1) Run `python3 runtime/scripts/fill_slates.py --books <that path>` — dry-run — and paste back the reel/beat list it prints. (2) Pick ONE slate beat from that list and open its parent beat_sheet.json. (3) Read the beat's narration and role_note; propose a REAL Remotion pattern (not FormACard) that would teach that narration — from `./art scenes` if a fit exists, or a new component if not. (4) Show me the exact diff you would make to `shot.remotion` for that one beat — do NOT run --apply.
output: step 1 — the printed reel/beat list, verbatim (no --apply)
step 2 — the chosen beat_id, its narration + role_note, and why it deserves better than a card
step 3 — the proposed pattern, either from ./art scenes or a new-component spec
